To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
P. phaselodes growth responses were influenced differently by specific combinations of arbuscular mychorrhizal fungi and rhizobacteria that solubilized calcium, iron, or aluminium phosphate.
the use of phosphate-solubilizers and mycorrhiza in combination may be a promising strategy for increasing plant growth, especially in low-P soils.
the plant —Rhizobia — mycorrhiza symbiosis system can increase in yield and in nutrition in association with bacteria that solublize calcium, iron and aluminium phosphates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system for the sustainable production of legume crops.

the development of a system that can improve the growth of leguminous forages in tropical acid soils, and the results suggest the possibility of using specific bacteria to enhance the effect of mycorrhiza on P uptake and yield.
the effects of specific rhizosphere bacterial groups in association with arbuscular myccorrhiza in legume crops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of the rhizosphere microorganisms are highly dependent upon the specific plant-microbe interactions, and the mechanisms involved in these associations need further elucidation.

the plant —rhizobia — mycorrhiza system may benefit from the addition of specific phosphate-solubilising bacteria, but the effect is dependent on both the plant, the fungus, and the bacterial species.

the plant—rhizobium—mycorrhiza symbiosis system is a promising alternative to the traditional use of chemical fertilizers, but that further studies are needed before the technology can be applied to the field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plant —Rhizobia — Glomus symbiosis can benefit in yield and nutrition when associated with specific rhizobacteria involved in P solubilisation.
the use of phosphate-solubilising bacteria may improve the efficiency of mycorrhiza in P acquisition by plants, especially when the mycorrhizae are less infective.
a specific combination of mycorrhiza, rhizobia, and P-solubizing bacteria can increase P nutrition and yield in P. phaseloids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a better understanding of the interactions between the different components involved in the P. phaseoloides —Rhizobum sp. — Glomus spp.— rhizosphere bacteria system will be necessary for its successful application to leguminous crops in the field.
the use of specific phosphate solubilizing bacteria and mycorrhiza may increase plant growth and nutrition in a more specific way than the use of generalist phosphate solubilizers.

the plant —Rhizobiium sp. — arbuscular mychorrhiza symbiosis system, in association with specific bacteria that solubolize calcium, iron and aluminium phosphates, may increase plant yield and nutrition.
